clue.text: In Homer's first poem I'll broadcast the subject of Keats?

indicators.note: the first letter of Homer is placed inside the scrambled letters
broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters of poem and I'll are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving three letters

indicators.note: the first of Homer's letters is the one wanted here

explanation.surface: A reader wonders whether Homer's first epic contains the theme of a Keats poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts H (Homer's first) inside an anagram of POEM + ILL, signalled by 'broadcast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Philomela in Greek myth became a nightingale, and Keats wrote an ode to that bird, so the poetic name for the bird fits.

clue.text: Hands grabbing edges of individual Indian dishes

indicators.note: the hands grab something, so the other letters are held inside that word

parts.note: paws is a colloquial word for hands

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, here of individual

explanation.surface: Someone's hands seize the rims of separate plates of Indian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts IL, the first and last letters of 'individual', inside PAWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaw is a variant spelling of pilaf, a spiced rice dish of South Asian and Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: Leaderless entries reprinted extra pages

indicators.note: a reprint can set the letters in a new order, so the remainder is rearranged
losing its leader means the word entries drops its opening letter

explanation.surface: A publisher reissues a directory without its first listings, adding extra pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' removes E from ENTRIES, and 'reprinted' rearranges NTRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose leaflet or extra section slipped into a magazine is called an insert, so these are added pages.

clue.text: Double blow that leads naturally to what's left here

definitions.text: Double blow that leads naturally to what's left here

parts.words: Double blow that leads naturally to what's left here
parts.note: a boxer's quick left-then-right pair of punches, also the counting words that come just before the number of this clue

explanation.surface: A boxer's combination of punches sets up a final left hook.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is 3-down, and counting 'one, two' leads naturally to three, the clue's own number; 'left' also suggests the boxer's left hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing a quick jab followed by a cross with the other hand is the classic double punch combination.

clue.text: Cover up talker that comes out with gas

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pave a path is to cover it with a surface
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A speaker hides the fact that he is full of hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PAVE into EVAP. The definition reads 'comes out with gas' as producing vapour rather than talking hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial evaporator turns liquid into vapour, so steam leaves it.

clue.text: Story associated with the German songs

parts.note: a story can be a fib, a lie
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A tale goes with some songs from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: German art songs of the Romantic era, by Schubert or Schumann, are known by the German plural term.

clue.text: Press needing help to identify content of velvet glove?

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
to lend a hand is to help

explanation.surface: A printing press needs assistance to work out what is inside a soft glove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like a newspaper or machine, but it is the verb for smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'an iron fist in a velvet glove' describes firm rule under a gentle manner, so the hard part sits inside.

clue.text: Journalist following duke on circuitous route deviated from main road

indicators.note: the journalist's letters come after the duke and the rearranged route
a circuitous path twists about, so the letters of route are rearranged

parts.note: ED, short for editor, stands for a journalist in crosswords

explanation.surface: A reporter tails a duke on a winding trip that has left the main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circuitous' rearranges ROUTE into ETOUR, and 'following' puts ED after D + ETOUR; 'on' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To detour is to take a roundabout way off the usual highway, so the past tense means went off it.

clue.text: One strives energetically and calls repeatedly

indicators.note: energetic movement throws the letters around into a fresh order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A single person keeps striving and phones over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energetically' rearranges I + STRIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes back to a place again pays further visits there, calling more than once.

clue.text: Gave out girl's seen around American resort

indicators.note: the girl's word goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a lass is a girl; the possessive adds S

indicators.note: out suggests the letters have gone awry and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman gave things away in a US holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GAVE into VEGA, and 'seen around' puts LASS around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city is famous as a gambling and entertainment destination in the United States.

clue.text: Mutilated torso, see, found in Don's place?

indicators.note: a mutilated thing is torn up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, in references

explanation.surface: A dismembered body has been found at a university don's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutilated' rearranges TORSO into ROSTO. 'Don' looks like a university teacher but is the Russian river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city of Rostov-on-Don stands on the Don river, so it is a place on the Don.

clue.text: Timber cross sections in infestation

indicators.note: the two sections of the word are swapped round, the front part moving to the end

parts.note: wood is timber
worm is an infestation of parasites, as when a pet has worms

explanation.surface: A carpenter looks at slices of timber riddled with pests.
explanation.walkthrough: WOOD + WORM gives WOODWORM, the timber pest; 'sections in' swaps its two halves. 'cross' is a burden, as in a cross to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood, a bitter herb, stands figuratively for bitterness and grief, a trial or affliction to bear.

clue.text: Mum polishes plants

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay quiet, and sh is the call for silence
to rub something is to polish it

explanation.surface: Mother is shining up the houseplants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means silence, as in keeping mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushes are woody garden plants, smaller than trees.

clue.text: Style affected by our Aunt Eva

indicators.note: letters affected by change are altered into a different order

explanation.surface: A design fashion is influenced by a relative named Eva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected by' rearranges OUR AUNT EVA.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorative movement of about 1890 to 1910, with flowing plant forms, is a recognised artistic style.

clue.text: Class of degree in Fine Art? He worked hard to enter it

indicators.note: hard goes into the middle of the rearranged letters
worked means reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An art graduate wonders about the grade of an art degree he earned by hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges FINE ART HE, and 'to enter' puts H inside it. 'degree' looks academic, but here it is a temperature unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fahrenheit is a scale used to measure temperature, so it is a type of degree.

clue.text: Bosuns worked in command beneath the boom

indicators.note: worked means reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: IC stands for in charge, in command

explanation.surface: Ship's officers labour under the orders of a captain below the sail's boom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges BOSUNS. 'boom' looks like a sail spar but is a sonic boom.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane flying below the speed of sound causes no sonic boom, so it stays under that threshold.

clue.text: Dream of stag Ares gave Zeus? Not half

indicators.note: only half of each word is used, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A dream of what a stag offered to the war god Ares, father Zeus not halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the first half of each of 'stag', 'Ares', 'gave' and 'Zeus' gives ST + AR + GA + ZE.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze at the stars idly is to be lost in daydreams.

clue.text: Parties around ten, that is, for lots of stars

indicators.note: the parties surround the other letters

parts.note: galas are festive parties
X is the Roman numeral for ten
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Celebrations at about ten o'clock attract plenty of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts X + IE inside GALAS. 'stars' suggests celebrities at a party but means huge groups of suns.
explanation.definitionFit: Each galaxy is an enormous system of millions of suns.

clue.text: Tiny waves evident in swirling old lunar dust

indicators.note: swirling dust churns the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Minute ripples show in moon dust that has been stirred up long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges O + LUNAR + DUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultrasonic sound has frequencies above human hearing and very short wavelengths.

clue.text: Performance in first part of play no good?

parts.note: a play's first part is Act I

explanation.surface: Is a show worthless in its opening act?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a role on stage is a dramatic performance.

clue.text: Writer I met in Paris and Rome

parts.note: je is French for I, the word one meets in Paris
the city is taken as written

explanation.surface: An author recalls meeting someone in Paris and Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerome K. Jerome wrote 'Three Men in a Boat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome was an English humorist and author.

clue.text: Tries prose compositions

explanation.surface: Attempts at writing pieces of prose.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it, and the noun names short prose pieces written on a subject.

clue.text: Spades came right off card

parts.note: S is short for spades, a suit of cards

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a card game, a spade came and then the right card left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CAME + R. 'card' suggests playing cards but means a comic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a witty or amusing person, and so is someone described as a scream.

clue.text: Friends eating cold duck more than once?

indicators.note: the Friends take the cold letter inside

parts.note: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Companions are eating cold duck repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friends' are the Quakers here. The definition imagines more than one duck's quack.
explanation.definitionFit: Quackers is a slang word for crazy and a playful plural for ducks, those that make the quacking sound.

clue.text: Vitamin damaged American Indian's heart

indicators.note: damage puts the letters into disarray
the heart of the phrase is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A vitamin harmed the heart of a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the middle six letters ICANIN from AMERICANINDIAN, and 'damaged' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotinic acid, one of the B vitamins, is known by this name.

clue.text: A commie's beaten up, in a half-conscious state

indicators.note: being beaten up knocks the letters about into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving COMMIES

explanation.surface: A communist has been beaten up and left barely conscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' rearranges COMMIES into SEMICOM, and the clue's opening A goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A partial coma is a state of reduced, partial consciousness.

clue.text: Bore VIP

explanation.surface: A dull person is in fact an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheese off is to bore or annoy, and a big cheese is a slang term for a very important person.

clue.text: More than one citizen's food rejected, by woman's son

definitions.note: citizen's stands for citizen is, so the plural is defined

indicators.note: rejected things are turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food
her is the possessive word for a woman

explanation.surface: A citizen's meal is turned down, all thanks to a woman's son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns GRUB into BURG.
explanation.definitionFit: Burghers are townsfolk, residents of a borough, especially in a medieval town.
